decisions.reason: As a close-to-core instrument kept on the home page across 2023 and 2024, it likely meets or exceeds aspirations and is cheap to retain within the firm's established QA portfolio.
This software builds on the firm's core oncology QA capabilities and, despite potentially slower customer adoption, an expanding innovative firm is likely to keep it while learning from the market.
The CT image quality phantom is adjacent to the firm's imaging QA direction, so with current organisational slack and only one year of market history management would probably continue it.
Because it is more distant from the established offer its performance is more uncertain, but in a growing firm with a broad portfolio management would usually allow more time before exiting.

This distant and relatively narrow mammography product faces the highest review risk, yet the firm's expansion and willingness to search in adjacent medical imaging niches still make retention more likely than withdrawal.
Medical imaging QA instruments fit the firm's capabilities in measurement, calibration and integrated QA, so they are likely to remain on the market unless early results are clearly below aspiration.
